assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational body of theory and experimental evidence made reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion central to modern economic analysis.
assessment.attribution: Fehr, Falk and Schmidt provide a coherent and highly influential experimental-theoretical attribution.
assessment.maturity: The research program has been tested across many settings and has reshaped labour, organizational and behavioural economics.
uncertainties: The broad intellectual lineage of social preferences makes any three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM supplied a widely used solution to a fundamental empirical identification problem in economics.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are the clearest attribution for the core estimator, with Blundell central to its major extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods have long been standard and their strengths and failure modes are well understood.
uncertainties: The appropriate laureate set depends on whether the prize emphasizes the original estimator or the system-GMM extension.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods transformed empirical analysis of forward-looking decisions and made structural dynamic programming operational.
assessment.attribution: Rust is the unmistakable central architect of the landmark framework; later contributors broadened it substantially.
assessment.maturity: The framework has endured for decades across labour, industrial organization and related fields.
uncertainties: Structural assumptions and computational burdens have generated continuing debate about the scope of empirical conclusions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm-heterogeneity trade theory changed how economists analyze trade, productivity, selection and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the singular essential attribution for the canonical model, while Helpman and Redding made important complementary contributions.
assessment.maturity: Its predictions and mechanisms have generated a large, sustained empirical and theoretical literature.
uncertainties: The contribution may be viewed as part of a broader sequence of modern trade advances rather than a separable discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of insurance theory with credible measurement clarified selection, pricing and welfare in consequential markets.
assessment.attribution: The listed scholars jointly represent the principal theoretical and empirical advances, although their roles are not identical.
assessment.maturity: The work is mature, empirically influential and directly relevant to health, credit and insurance policy.
uncertainties: A single prize citation may have difficulty encompassing the distinct theoretical and applied strands.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental markets and behavioural game theory established durable tools for testing strategic behaviour and institutional predictions.
assessment.attribution: Plott, Holt and Camerer are prominent contributors to the experimental and behavioural program, though the field has many indispensable pioneers.
assessment.maturity: The approaches have accumulated extensive replication, methodological refinement and application over several decades.
uncertainties: The breadth of the field makes the three-person limit and a unified prize citation difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative-data research supplied influential measures of intergenerational mobility and evidence on its geographic and policy determinants.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman form a plausible core for the major linked contributions.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been highly consequential and extensively extended, though the program remains comparatively recent.
uncertainties: Interpretation of mobility measures and causal implications remains actively contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of ambiguity aversion provided a major alternative to subjective expected utility and influenced decision, finance and economic theory.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa and Epstein are central to the canonical maxmin formulation, with Marinacci an important contributor to the broader literature.
assessment.maturity: The axiomatic foundations are long established and their influence is broad.
uncertainties: The empirical importance and uniquely appropriate attribution of competing ambiguity models remain uncertain.
